app.title: Local AI Model Manager
app.subtitle: Local model lifecycle management with an OpenAI-compatible gateway
page.models.title: Models
page.models.desc: Register, edit and run models. Starting the manager loads no models; a model loads on demand when an API request arrives.
page.runtimeStatus.title: Runtime Status
page.runtimeStatus.desc: A live view of the gateway, loaded models, engine processes and VRAM usage.
page.runtimeLogs.title: Runtime Logs
page.runtimeLogs.desc: In-memory logs (nothing is written to disk by default). API keys, authentication headers, full prompts and outputs are never logged by default.
page.apiIntegration.title: API Integration
page.apiIntegration.desc: The currently effective connection details and copy-ready examples. All examples are generated live from the current settings and the selected model.
page.settingsGeneral.title: General
page.settingsGeneral.desc: Startup behavior, language and theme. Models always stay in standby and are never loaded automatically when Windows starts.
page.settingsApi.title: API
page.settingsApi.desc: Listen address, port and authentication for the OpenAI-compatible gateway. Bound to the loopback address by default.
page.settingsEngine.title: Inference Engine
page.settingsEngine.desc: Register, switch and upgrade inference engines. Engines can be replaced independently; model records reference only an engine ID.
page.settingsModelParameters.title: Model Parameters
page.settingsModelParameters.desc: Only the most common parameters are exposed; all other llama.cpp parameters go under “Other parameters”, one per line. Unchecked/empty parameters are not passed to the engine — VRAM is decided by the model and the engine's own defaults, not by this app for you.
page.settingsLifecycle.title: Lifecycle
page.settingsLifecycle.desc: On-demand loading, idle unload, and the eviction policy used when VRAM runs short.
page.settingsResources.title: Resources
page.settingsResources.desc: VRAM / CPU sampling and the value policy used by auto-tune.
page.settingsNetwork.title: Network
page.settingsNetwork.desc: Internal engine ports and the outbound proxy. Internal ports always bind to the loopback address only and are never exposed externally.
page.settingsAdvanced.title: Advanced
page.settingsAdvanced.desc: Logging, request limits and experimental switches. Logs are kept in memory only by default.

params.section.other: Other parameters (advanced; write llama.cpp parameters directly, one per line)
params.other.hint: Examples: --some-option value / --another-option (a flag that takes no value goes on its own line). These lines are appended to the llama-server command line as-is; --model / --host / --port are managed by the manager and are ignored if written here.
params.footer.core: Core rule: unchecked = not sent. This app never fills in inference parameters for you; VRAM usage is determined by the model and llama.cpp's own defaults.
params.footer.defaults: Note llama.cpp's own defaults: without --n-gpu-layers, -ngl = 0 (CPU only); without --ctx-size it uses the model's own training context, and the KV cache is reserved in one block for that context, so a long-context model can consume well over ten GB of VRAM.
params.footer.autotune: If you would rather not compute this yourself, use “Auto-tune” on the “Models” page — it reads the GGUF metadata and suggests values based on VRAM, but only when you explicitly ask for it.
params.footer.restart: After you save, a loaded model picks up the new parameters only after you click “Restart” on the “Models” page.

param.ctx-size.name: Context length
param.ctx-size.desc: Prompt context length (tokens). When unset, llama.cpp decides — it uses the model's own training context; the KV cache is reserved in one block for that context (for a 32-layer / 4 KV-head model in this project, roughly 64 KB per token, so a 256K context means 16 GiB). Set it explicitly to control VRAM.
param.n-gpu-layers.name: GPU layers (offload)
param.n-gpu-layers.desc: Number of layers offloaded to the GPU. When unset, llama.cpp's own default applies, i.e. 0 (CPU only). Use 99 (or all) to offload every layer to the GPU, or 0 to explicitly use the CPU.
param.threads.name: CPU threads
param.threads.desc: Number of CPU threads used during generation. When unset, llama.cpp decides.
param.batch-size.name: Logical batch size
param.batch-size.desc: Logical batch size (tokens). When unset, the engine default applies.
param.ubatch-size.name: Physical (U) batch size
param.ubatch-size.desc: Physical micro-batch size. Lowering it reduces peak VRAM during prompt processing. When unset, the engine default applies.
param.cache-type-k.name: KV cache type (K)
param.cache-type-k.desc: Quantizing the K part of the KV cache significantly reduces VRAM usage (q8_0 roughly halves it). When unset, the engine default f16 applies.
param.cache-type-v.name: KV cache type (V)
param.cache-type-v.desc: Quantizes the V part; some builds require flash attention to be enabled as well. When unset, the engine default f16 applies.

resources.autoTuneContext.label: Target context for auto-tune
resources.autoTuneContext.help: Auto-tune sizes the context to this value rather than “as much as VRAM can hold”. The KV cache is reserved in one block for the context, so this value directly determines VRAM usage: a 1.8B model needs about 0.5 GiB of KV at 8192 and about 8 GiB at 131072. Default 8192.
resources.maxVramUsage.label: Per-model VRAM safety limit
resources.maxVramUsage.help: A safety valve only: used to shrink the context when even the target context does not fit. It is not a “use as much as possible” target. Default 70%.
